sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by Alexa-647-conjugated anti-M1 FLAG antibody flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells; receptor traffics to the cell surface. Functional readout (e.g., cAMP, Gs coupling) not reported in the ledger clips for this tagged construct.
sites.rationale: GPR161 has no endogenous signal peptide; its N-terminus (residue 1, M) is extracellular (topology landmarks: EXTRACELLULAR 1–30, TM1 31–52). The published construct prepends an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by FLAG before residue 1, so insert_after_residue=0 with residue_after=M is the only possible junction — there is exactly one extracellular terminus and no ambiguity. Python verification confirms seq[0]='M' and TM1 begins at position 31, leaving 30 extracellular residues downstream of the tag. Surface display is directly confirmed by anti-FLAG flow cytometry on intact (non-permeabilized) cells in three independent publications. Full-length human GPR161 expressed in HEK293 cells with an exogenous HA signal peptide prepended and a FLAG epitope tag (DYKDDDDA) placed between the HA-SP cleavage site and GPR161 residue 1 (M), in a tetracycline-inducible pcDNA3.1 vector. GPR161 carries no endogenous signal peptide (topology begins O at residue 1); the HA-SP drives membrane insertion and is cleaved, leaving FLAG at the extracellular N-terminus before residue 1. Surface display confirmed by anti-M1 FLAG antibody flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells (L4/L5/L6). The same construct architecture is independently reported in at least three publications (L1, L2, L3, L7).

sources.claim: Expression and purification of GPR161 active-state complex The human GPR161 gene with an N-terminal influenza hemagglutinin signal sequence and FLAG epitope was cloned into a pcDNA3.1 vector with zeocin resistance and a tetracycline inducible cassette, as described previously 66 .

literature_notes: L1/L2/L3/L7 all describe the same N-terminal HA-SP+FLAG construct for full-length membrane-anchored GPR161; L4/L5/L6 confirm surface display of that construct by flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells. L7 states the construct was used for 'functional and surface-expression studies' but reports no specific functional result in the ledger clip, so validation_level is capped at surface_only. L8/L9 (C-terminal GFP on mouse Gpr161) and L10 (C-terminal miniGs399 fusion) are placed in other_positions because the C-terminus of GPR161 is intracellular (topology: INTRACELLULAR 327–529). No ledger line supports an insertion in any extracellular loop (ECL1 86–101, ECL2 167–187, ECL3 293–305), so no internal sites are proposed.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal GFP fusion on full-length mouse Gpr161 stably expressed in NIH 3T3 Flp-In fibroblasts; the C-terminus (residue 529, R) lies in the intracellular region (topology: INTRACELLULAR 327–529), so this is not a surface tag site.
C-terminal miniGs399 fusion (preceded by a GS linker and 3C protease site) on full-length human GPR161 for active-state structural studies; C-terminus is intracellular, not a surface tag site.
